sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for randomly formed groups under fixed group sizes and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

body.tldr: Randomly formed groups behave unlike independent regression clusters once a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The exact normalized Kneser operator yields a finite-sample design-variance identity and a dense limit in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives. A two-permutation martingale then gives centered design-based Gaussian inference under predictable-variation stabilization. The familiar equal-group CR2 statistic consistently estimates the independent-group term, so it is valid but conservative in the dense regime and ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible; when the sampling fraction vanishes, this recovers studentized normality without the birthday restriction \(N_n^2/n\to0\). An enumerable eight-unit design verifies the factor-two variance excess. For growing group counts, a stable treatment fraction, and a positive limiting sampling fraction, two equal-observation Rademacher priors have separated positive scaled-variance limits. Exact one-realization variance recovery over the full dense class is posed honestly as an open question whose remaining step is a filtration-specific predictable-quadratic-variation and deterministic-diagonal argument for those priors.

project_justification.gap: FuSamiiWang2026 defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws, which requires \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation loses first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while the fixed-cluster CR2 literature has no mechanism for restoring it.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so the exact causal variance can be decomposed by Johnson degree before treatment randomization is averaged out. This exposes a scalar sampling-fraction phase transition that whole-tuple coupling cannot see.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale, obtains a centered martingale CLT, characterizes CR2 conservativeness and ratio consistency, verifies the exact software statistic and finite witness, and isolates the remaining all-statistic lower-bound lemma as a first-class open object.

body.related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 defines the homogeneous-group PAME, Theorems 1--2 prove asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under \(N_n^2/n\to0\), and Section 4.1 transports an independent-group limit through whole-tuple total variation. The sparse-beyond-birthday theorem replaces that birthday condition by statistic-specific predictable-variation stabilization, while the dense theorem retains the dependence their coupling removes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic eigenspace architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies an explicit classical spectrum source, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form rather than attributing that step to either paper. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform the complete-randomization component conditional on a partition. \cite{Ohlsson1989} and \cite{Chao1997} inform the two-stage and permutation-martingale route, with the grouped unit-then-label predictable variation remaining design-specific. Theorem 1 and Appendix A of \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explain CR2 working-model calibration under independent clusters; \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. Neither paper is claimed to cover the random-partition correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} characterizes optimized conservative quadratic bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; they inform, but do not subsume, the proposed equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias equals \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. The Rademacher variance limits are separated only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their limit gap is zero. The proposed uniform impossibility is not counted as a theorem contribution until the two explicit Rademacher priors are shown to satisfy the same predictable-variation condition as the centered CLT under the exact reveal order.
body.honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, dense projection limit, bounded-increment lemma, centered CLT conditional on predictable-variation stabilization, CR2 frontier, sparse reduction, software equality, eight-unit witness, and equal-observation Rademacher variance separation are theorem targets. The Rademacher separation assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\); its smaller scaled-variance limit is at least \(2/M\), so the prior rows obey scaled-variance nondegeneracy with high probability for every fixed lower bound below that limit. The high-probability predictable-variation verification for both Rademacher priors, diagonal selection into deterministic arrays, and resulting uniform all-statistic lower bound remain the open-ended question. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and the Rademacher limit gap vanish, and the result reduces to the known sparse PAME variance and CR2 studentization; when \(\rho>0\), no finite-sample conservativeness claim is made.
